Article Title: Centre turns up heat on Zakir Naik: States, UTs get sweeping powers under UAPA to act against banned IRF
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik 's Islamic Research Foundation IRF ), empowering state governments and Union Territory administrations to freeze funds and restrict access to properties linked to the organisation. The move comes days after the home ministry extended a five-year ban on the IRFAccording to a notification issued on Thursday, the Centre has delegated these powers to states and UTs under Section 42 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA)."The Central Government hereby directs that all powers exercisable by it under sections 7 and 8 of the UAPA shall also be exercised by the state governments and the Union territory administrations in relation to the above said unlawful association,” the notification said.The notification also refers to the Centre's November 13 declaration of the IRF as an unlawful association under the UAPA. "In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 3 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (37 of 1967), the Central Government has declared the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), as an unlawful association vide notification number, S.O. 6182(E), dated the 13th November"Section 7 of the UAPA empowers the government to prohibit the use of funds belonging to an association declared unlawful. It allows authorities to issue a written order barring anyone holding money, securities or credits being used, or intended to be used, for the association from paying, transferring or otherwise dealing with them without the government's written permission.A government-appointed gazetted officer can also be authorised to inspect the person's premises, examine records and investigate financial transactions suspected to be linked to the unlawful association.Section 8, meanwhile, empowers the government to notify any place, including a house, building or part of it, a tent or a vessel, that it believes is being used for the purposes of an unlawful association.Following such a notification, the district magistrate can prepare an inventory of movable property at the premises and prohibit the use of articles suspected to be connected with the association. The magistrate can also restrict entry into the notified premises by people who were not residents there when the notification was issued. Police officers of at least the rank of sub-inspector can search people entering or found at the premises.
Article Summary: The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation IRF. State governments and Union Territory administrations can freeze funds and restrict access to properties linked to the organisation. The move comes days after the home ministry extended a five-year ban on the IRF

Article Title: PM Modi to hold key cabinet meet at 1 pm; tweaks to delimitation-linked women's quota Bill on agenda
Article Text:
Centre may delink delimitation from Census and consider a 50% seat increase across states.

NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is scheduled to meet on Friday to discuss the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill, ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, sources told ANI.The meeting has been convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to ensure their presence. According to new agency ANI, The government is likely to consider amendments to the earlier version of the legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.The reported discussions come amid indications that the government is exploring changes to the delimitation framework, including a proposal to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50% across all states and retain their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.According to PTI, the proposed formula is aimed at addressing concerns, particularly among southern states, over the impact of delimitation on their parliamentary representation. However, no final decision has been taken.Some media reports have also suggested that the government may consider delinking delimitation from the Census, potentially allowing the exercise to proceed without waiting for the next Census figures.The special sitting of Parliament is scheduled to begin with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.The proposed legislation follows the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha in April. The bill sought to link the implementation of 33% women's reservation in legislatures with delimitation and proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats.
Article Summary: The meeting has been convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to ensure their presence. The government is likely to consider amendments to the earlier version of the legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.

Article Title: Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days
Article Text:
Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati informed a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalay Bagchi and V Mohana that in the 22 cases, HDFC, ICICI, Samman and PNB have granted conditional sanction for prosecution

Once sanction is granted, courts will expeditiously take cognisance of CBI chargesheets, start trial: SC

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has read out the riot act and asked HDFC Bank ICICI Bank , Sammaan Capital and PNB Home Finance to grant unconditional sanction within a week to prosecute their bank officials, who are charged by CBI for colluding with builders in the alleged duping of homebuyers under the subvention schemes, or remain present in court to explain the lapse.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati said CBI, as directed by the SC, had inquired into 55 cases pan-India and has filed chargesheets in 22 cases, closed 3 cases and expects to complete the probe into the rest in three months.Bhati informed a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalay Bagchi and V Mohana that in the 22 cases, HDFC, ICICI, Samman and PNB have granted conditional sanction for prosecution, which is creating doubts in the minds of trial courts in taking cognisance of the chargesheet and proceeding with framing of charges.When senior advocate Sanjiv Sen, appearing for HDFC, said that sanction has been granted but there are certain rulings of the constitutional courts that flag the issue of whether private bank officials are public servants requiring sanction for prosecution. Moreover, the officials charged have been exonerated of wrongdoing in the internal inquiry, Sen said.The CJI-led bench said what else but exoneration of officials is expected in internal inquiries by banks, which had hobnobbed with rogue builders and cheated the homebuyers by releasing large sums of loan instalments to the builders even when there was hardly any progress in the construction of housing projects.When Sen protested against grant of sanction citing a judgment, the bench differentiated and said this is a court-monitored investigation, and hence SC can direct the banks to grant unconditional sanction for prosecution of delinquent officials.The bench said, “We direct all banks to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within a week, failing which their CMDs shall remain present in court to explain why action should not be taken against them.”The bench said once the sanction is granted, the trial courts will expeditiously take cognisance of CBI chargesheets and begin trial as per law. It also directed CBI to conclude investigations into the remaining cases expeditiously and not later than two months.On Aug 6, SC said that in court-monitored investigations, sanction for prosecution should be granted promptly and directed the banks to give necessary permissions within two weeks for prosecution of the accused bank officials. “Failure to accord sanction within two weeks would require banks to submit explanations to the court,” it had said and asked the CBI to share documents on the money trail with the ED to kick off an inquiry under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has asked HDFC Bank ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Home Finance to grant unconditional sanction to prosecute their bank officials. The officials are charged by CBI for colluding with builders in the alleged duping of homebuyers under the subvention schemes.

Article Title: ‘105 days of Operation Lotus’: Opposition targets Centre over special Parliament sitting amid delimitation bill buzz
Article Text:
File photo

Congress alleges attempt to secure numbers for Constitution amendment

CPI(M) MP alleges political manoeuvring to push delimitation

What is behind the special sitting?

NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Thursday criticised the Centre's decision to convene a special sitting of Parliament from November 30, alleging that the move was aimed at securing the numbers to pass the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment Bill that was defeated in April.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the Narendra Modi government of attempting to manufacture a two-thirds majority after what he described as "105 days of Operation Lotus", while Congress MP Manish Tewari said the proposed sitting mocked Parliament and should not replace the regular Winter Session.Communist Party of India (Marxist) MP John Brittas also alleged that the government was using political manoeuvring to secure support for delimitation under the cover of the Women's Reservation Bill.The reactions came after Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business. The sittings may conclude on December 3, depending on the business, he said.In a post on X, Ramesh linked the announcement to the government's earlier attempt to pass the delimitation-linked legislation, which failed to secure the required majority in April."On the evening of Ambedkar Jayanti on April 14, 2026, the Modi Govt had made the Delimitation Bills public that met their well-deserved fate on the night of April 17, 2026."Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi Govt announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill. Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution?"The fight is on," he wrote.Tewari, the Congress MP from Chandigarh, questioned the decision to convene a special sitting instead of a regular Winter Session."This request mocks the institution of Parliament. It is time for the Winter Session to convene. A special session is a mechanism for convening sitting during the inter-session period. It can and should not become a substitute for a regular Winter Session," he said in a post tagging Rijiju."Why not just convene a regular Winter Session when the government can, if it chooses, 'regurgitate' defeated legislation," he added.The proposed sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not been formally prorogued.Brittas alleged that the government was attempting to secure a parliamentary majority through political mergers and defections to push through the delimitation exercise."Modi Govt's so-called amalgamations, takeovers, mergers and buyouts appear to have one sinister objective: manufacture a majority to push through delimitation under the guise of the Women's Reservation Bill. The real 'expenditure' for the session will be humongous!!" he wrote on X.He also cautioned against using women's empowerment as a cover for changes to the country's electoral framework."A majority manufactured through political manipulation is not a mandate. It is a mockery of democracy. If this is how India's electoral future is being reshaped, the special session of Parliament on November 30 could mark the saddest chapter in the history of Indian democracy. Women's empowerment must never become a smokescreen for electoral engineering," Brittas added.Congress MP Karti P Chidambaram, meanwhile, appeared to suggest that the BJP may have secured the support of the DMK and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) for the proposed legislation."Guess the BJP government has got its ducks in a row!" he wrote on X, tagging the official accounts of the BJP, DMK and NCP-SP.However, NCP-SP MP Shashikant Shinde said his party would decide its position only after examining the proposed legislation."There is a lot of discussion today about what delimitation might look like, but no bill or proposal has been presented yet. Once the proposal is introduced in the session, our party's MPs will study it and discuss it in Parliament," he said.Shinde added that party leaders Supriya Sule and Amol Kolhe would decide the party's position and course of action after the details were made available.Sule had also recently said it would be premature to oppose the delimitation Bill before its contents were known. "Let the bill come. Perhaps there could be something good in the Delimitation Bill," she told news agency PTI.The announcement has renewed speculation that the government may reintroduce the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation and facilitate the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in legislatures.The Bill, introduced in April along with the Delimitation Bill, 2026 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17.A constitutional amendment requires the support of at least 361 members in the present 543-member House. With three vacancies, the Lok Sabha currently has 540 members. The ruling NDA has around 320 MPs and would need additional support to cross the threshold.The political arithmetic has changed since the Bill's defeat. According to the PTI background report, 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP-SP, with eight, could also play a role in the numbers required.The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, according to sources.A Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group meeting is also scheduled for Friday to discuss the party's approach to the parliamentary sitting.The opposition INDIA bloc has demanded that the 33 per cent women's reservation be implemented in the existing 543-member Lok Sabha, without linking it to delimitation.The government, meanwhile, has maintained that delimitation is necessary to reflect updated population data and facilitate the implementation of the quota.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday reiterated his commitment to women's representation, saying no force could prevent the government from ensuring justice for women. He also blamed an opposition party for the defeat of the Constitution amendment Bill in April.
Article Summary: Congress alleges attempt to secure numbers for Constitution amendment.CPI(M) MP alleges political manoeuvring to push delimitation. Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30.

NEW DELHI: Netflix’s first original Pakistan i series has run into a diplomatic and regulatory hurdle in India even before its global premiere. The ministry of information and broadcasting on Thursday asked the streaming giant to ensure that no content originating in Pakistan is made available to Indian subscribers, following complaints over the possible release of its star-studded romantic drama, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo.Scheduled for release on December 4, the series features Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Sanam Saeed and Hania Aamir, actors familiar to Indian audiences. Netflix has not clarified whether India is among the markets where the series will be streamed.The ministry’s intervention comes 18 months after government, amid Operation Sindoor, issued an advisory on May 8, 2025, asking digital platforms to discontinue Pakistani-origin films, series, songs, podcasts and other content on national security grounds.Officials said Netflix had informed the ministry in June 2025 that no Pakistani-origin film or series was available to its Indian subscribers. The ministry has now asked it to honour that commitment.When TOI reached out to Netflix, the platform said it had no comment.The controversy escalated after All Indian Cine Workers Association and Federation of Western India Cine Employees approached PM Narendra Modi. All Indian Cine Workers Association has also sought a permanent legal framework prohibiting Pakistani entertainment content in India, while Federation of Western India Cine Employees, an umbrella body of 32 associations representing five lakh workers, threatened to “ensure the shoot of all Netflix projects comes to a halt” if the series is released.Pakistan’s planning and development minister, Ahsan Iqbal, accused India of weaponising art and culture.Directed and produced by Momina Duraid, the series is based on Farhat Ishtiaq’s bestselling 2013 Urdu novel.

Article Title: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
Article Text:
HC’s verdict came on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the Oct 2022 order of the home ministry cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate.

Delhi HC: No proof of ‘ anti-government activism ’ charge against NGO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking a dim view of the home ministry’s reluctance to share even with the court the inputs that led it to cancel the FCRA licence of an NGO engaged in legal aid, Delhi high court on Thursday set aside the decision. HC said the move to cancel the licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC) based solely on the allegation that it has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was without any material.HC said no material was furnished by government to show that SLIC’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity or security of India or the public interest.While government contends that the violations on the appellant’s NGO’s part were brought to its notice through ‘security inputs’, which cannot be divulged since they are ‘secret’; this court is of the view that such inputs cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is brought even to the notice of this court, though the appellant has faced the drastic action of having its FCRA registration cancelled, arising from such inputs,” Justice AJ Bhambhani of Delhi HC said.“The respondent’s (Centre) allegation that the appellant has indulged in ‘aggressive anti-government political activism’ is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation,” HC added in its judgement.It said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in “political activity” or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains.“In the impugned cancellation order, the respondent has also alleged that the appellant’s activities amount to an attempt to portray a ‘wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community’. This court would observe that this allegation strains credulity; and this court is dismayed by the respondent’s attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light,” it said.HC’s verdict came on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the Oct 2022 order of the home ministry cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country.
Article Summary: HC’s verdict came on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the Oct 2022 order of the home ministry cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. Delhi high court said the move to cancel the licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC) based solely on the allegation that it has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was without any material.

Article Title: 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock
Article Text:
Taking note of the report filed by the mediator, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran closed the mediation. “One can never force a settlement,” it observed.

NEW DELHI: Seven months of mediation proceedings, which were conducted on the direction of the SC for amicable resolution of the property dispute between late industrialist Sunjay Kapur’s mother, Rani Kapur, and his widow, Priya Sachdev Kapur, fell flat, and the former CJI DY Chandrachud, who was the mediator, told the court Thursday that the mediation reached an impasse despite 15 sittings.He was roped in by the SC in May to settle the high-profile property dispute between them over Kapur’s Rs 30,000 crore estate.Taking note of the report filed by the mediator, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran closed the mediation. “One can never force a settlement,” it observed.As the lawyers appearing for the Kapurs blamed each other’s clients for mediation failure, the bench told the parties, “When you all decide to sit, talk, and try to find a way out, you need to show some flexibility, some understanding, and take a practical view of the matter... 15 sittings and you all couldn’t reach a conclusion.”The court said that it would pass a short order in the case.
Article Summary: Seven months of mediation proceedings between late industrialist Sunjay Kapur’s mother, Rani Kapur, and his widow, Priya Sachdev Kapur fell flat. Former CJI DY Chandrachud, who was the mediator, told the court Thursday that the mediation reached an impasse despite 15 sittings.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of information and broadcasting asked Netflix to ensure that content originating in Pakistan is not streamed in India, in line with its May 8, 2025 order.According to sources quoted by ANI News agency, the ministry has asked Netflix to honour the commitment it made in June last year, when the streaming platform informed it that no film or series originating in Pakistan had been made available to subscribers in India.It has also asked Netflix to maintain the position it had conveyed at the time, sources told ANI.In June last year, Netflix informed the ministry that it had made no film or series originating in Pakistan available to subscribers in India.The direction comes after the ministry received several complaints and representations over the possible release in India of Pakistan-based web series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'.On Wednesday, Indian film industry bodies urged the government to prevent the web series' release in the country. Article Title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
Article Text:
Saying a consumer in India was entitled to 'no less protection and no less information' than one in the US or UK, SC said, 'We would urge such multinational FBOs to adopt uniform standards across jurisdictions.'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday called out the “double standard” of multinational companies in producing foodstuff for Indian consumers inferior in quality to what they did in Western countries, saying it was “deeply troubling”.While directing FSSAI to enforce front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) to make consumers aware of the contents of packaged food, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran deliberated on the dual yardsticks MNCs follow.“Concerns have been raised that certain multinational FBOs operating in India adopt practices towards Indian consumers that differ from those they follow elsewhere, including in the composition of their products and in the information provided on their labels. Such companies comply with, and in some instances voluntarily adopt, FoPNL requirements in other jurisdictions, yet resist similar measures here. If true, such double standards are deeply troubling,” the bench said.Saying a consumer in India was entitled to “no less protection and no less information” than one in the US or UK, SC said, “We would urge such multinational FBOs to adopt uniform standards across jurisdictions, and to extend to Indian consumers the same regard and respect for their health that they extend to consumers elsewhere.”It also directed FSSAI to ensure FBOs do not conceal or alter the composition of their products, or add additives, artificial preservatives, emulsifiers, etc, to soften the effect of FoPNL. “The introduction of a warning label must not become an occasion for reformulation that is hidden from the consumer, or that places the consumer at comparable or greater risk,” SC said.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran deliberated on the dual yardsticks MNCs follow. “Concerns have been raised that certain multinational FBOs operating in India adopt practices towards Indian consumers that differ from those they follow elsewhere,” they said.

Article Title: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions.

NEW DELHI: In an important insertion into the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, the Supreme Court on Friday said the bench of the adjudicating authority (AA), tasked with deciding the confirmation of ED’s orders for provisional attachment of assets by terming them proceeds of crime, must have a judicial member.Deciding a host of petitions questioning the competence of administrative members forming single-member benches to decide questions of law and conflicting judgements from various HCs, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions.“The presence of a judicial member on the bench undertaking the same ensures legal objectivity in the determination recorded by the AA. The lifetime of experience of the administrative and financial members in the AA would undoubtedly render them to be exceptional experts in their fields, but impartial and legally sound adjudication necessitates judicial temperament and training,” the bench said.It added, however, that the judgment would operate prospectively and not provide grounds for the reopening of past decisions.
Article Summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions. The presence of a judicial member on the bench ensures legal objectivity in the determination recorded by the AA.

Separate directives for reconvening the Houses were issued by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan.The special sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, as Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 but the session was not prorogued.Meanwhile, the Congress has issued a whip to its MPs in both Houses, asking them to remain present during the special sitting. The party has also directed its MPs to reach New Delhi by November 29, a day before the Lok Sabha reconvenes.The Congress on Friday alleged that the proposed sitting was primarily aimed at pushing delimitation and had little to do with women's reservation. Describing it as a desperate move by a "nervous and rattled PM who is under siege", the party said it would oppose the move with firm resolve.The DMK has also reiterated its opposition to any change in the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats among states. Article Title: India wins the Visitors’ Lion at the 61st Venice Art Biennale as NMACC anchors a historic return
Article Text:
“The National Pavilion of India at La Biennale di Venezia, features some of our most compelling artistic voices. This project underscores our vision for

art and culture

to foster a global dialogue that transcends boundaries, bringing the best of India and the world together.”

Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home

In Minor Keys

India has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, capping a triumphant return after a seven-year hiatus. Decided by public vote, the honour recognises a pavilion that drew roughly 4.5 lakh visitors at the Arsenale.At the heart of this milestone sits the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC), whose institutional muscle, championed by Founder and Chairperson Nita Ambani and Director Isha Ambani, placed contemporary Indian art squarely at the centre of global dialogue.For Isha Ambani, the victory marks a defining chapter in NMACC’s founding ambition.Speaking on the pavilion’s significance, she said:That vision was evident from opening week in May, when Isha Ambani co-hosted a landmark dinner at Venice’s Scuola Grande della Misericordia alongside curator Dr. Amin Jaffer, with Nita Ambani in attendance. Gathering international museum directors, curators, and collectors, the evening also highlighted how NMACC’s Mumbai programming feeds India’s global footprint, with exhibiting artists Asim Waqif and Ranjani Shettar having previously shown at Art House, NMACC.Presented by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre and Serendipity Arts Foundation, and curated by Dr. Amin Jaffer, the National Pavilion of India showcased the exceptional works of Alwar Balasubramaniam, Ranjani Shettar, Sumakshi Singh, Skarma Sonam Tashi and Asim Waqif. Titled, the exhibition responded to the Biennale’s theme,, examining belonging through Tamil Nadu clay, embroidered thread, botanical sculptures, Ladakhi papier-mâché, and bamboo.Complemented by Serendipity Arts’ city-wide performance programme, this public-voted triumph sets a formidable benchmark ahead of the Ministry of Culture’s upcoming The India Biennale, opening in New Delhi on 4 December 2026 across heritage sites including Purana Qila and the Red Fort.

NEW DELHI: The Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP will support the NDA government's push for the Delimitation Bill in Parliament, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told news agency ANI on Friday.The support from the YSRCP will strengthen the NDA's numbers as the Centre prepares to bring the legislation back to Parliament during a special sitting.Party sources told ANI that the YSRCP would support the Bill if it is introduced with provisions "ensuring regional balance."The development assumes significance as the government seeks to secure the two-thirds majority required to pass the legislation, which failed to clear the floor test during the Budget Session.Apart from the YSRCP, Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) has also adopted a softer stance on the proposed legislation. Article Title: Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises 16-year-old Indian AI entrepreneur
Article Text:
Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision

Putin's praise comes days after US trade body targets 'Make in India'

Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India'?

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ' Make in India ' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference. Putin and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev interacted with young innovators at the conference, where Aju, the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies, was among those introduced to the Russian president.During the interaction, Putin acknowledged Aju's work and highlighted how young innovators developing their own technological solutions contribute to the objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative."Ultimately your work helps realize PM Modi's "Make in India" call right? Because it helps young people find their own solutions and implement these solutions," Putin told Aju.Putin's remarks come days after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) criticised India's manufacturing and export policies, including the 'Make in India' initiative, in a report examining structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.In its Section 301 investigation report into India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors, the USTR alleged that India had adopted several measures that contributed to excess manufacturing capacity and production while failing to effectively address the resulting global concerns."India engages in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to the structural excess capacity and production evident in the indicia described above. Key among these are the umbrella efforts of Make in India, PLI, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), and IBEF, with a particular emphasis on efforts related to or under these efforts in the steel, solar, health, and ICT sectors," the USTR said.The report specifically identified the government's flagship 'Make in India' programme, Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) among the measures it said contributed to structural excess capacity.Popularly known online as 'Raul the Rockstar' and often described as the 'AI Kid of India', Aju is a teenager from Kerala who has pursued artificial intelligence despite coming from a Commerce background rather than a conventional engineering or computer science pathway.According to information shared on his LinkedIn profile, his interest in technology began when he was around nine years old. What started as independent learning and experimentation gradually developed into AI projects, educational initiatives and a growing online community.Aju studied Plus Two Commerce at North Edappally GHSS while simultaneously working on artificial intelligence projects. His LinkedIn profile identifies him as the founder and CTO of AIRealm Technologies, where he develops AI products and practical technology solutions.Projects associated with him include ThinkCraft, RESQ AI and MeBot, among other AI-based tools. He is also associated with ThinkCraft Academy, an AI learning platform that introduces students and professionals to emerging technologies.Beyond developing software, Aju has conducted AI workshops and sessions for students, educators and professionals, with a focus on making the technology accessible to people without technical backgrounds."I build things with AI. I talk about them. Sometimes I break them. Then I build them again," he writes in his LinkedIn introduction.His profile also states that he has delivered eight TEDx talks and conducted sessions at IITs, universities, schools and other institutions. He has built an online following of more than 500,000 people, sharing content related to artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju. Putin linked Aju's efforts in artificial intelligence to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' initiative. Aju is the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies.

Article Title: Trusts move HC to block chair’s casting vote at Tata Sons meet
Article Text:
Tata Sons board resolution on Chandrasekaran reappointment invalid, says Tata Trusts

Chandra set to chair board for most resolutions, giving him casting vote

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI:The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and R D Tata Trust (RDTT) have moved the Bombay high court to block the Tata Sons chairman from using his casting vote to break a tie on resolutions involving the Trusts' nominee directors at the Nov 30 board meeting, escalating the governance battle over control of India's largest conglomerate by revenue.The two trusts also want N Chandrasekaran 's reappointment as chairman declared invalid, arguing that the process violated Tata Sons' articles and have claimed Rs 65 crore in damages from the company and its board, except Noel Tata, plus 18% annual interest until payment.Senior counsel Abhishek Manu Singhvi and Janak Dwarkadas mentioned the two suits on Thursday and sought an urgent hearing because of Monday's board meeting. Justice Arif Doctor recused. Justice Abhay Ahuja then agreed to hear the matter on Friday, with Singhvi joining virtually.The suits, filed by SDTT through trustee Bhaskar Bhat and by RDTT through Rishi Sharma, head of legal at Tata Trusts, said Tata Sons used the chairman's casting vote to push through a resolution at the last board meeting on Sept 17, when the Trusts' two nominee directors split.According to the suits, Noel and Venu Srinivasan voted against and in favour, respectively, on Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Independent director Harish Manwani, who chaired that item after Chandrasekaran recused himself, used his casting vote to carry it.The Trusts fear the same device will be used on Nov 30 to push through resolutions including conversion of Tata Sons into a public company and its listing, amendments to its articles and an EGM on Chandrasekaran's reappointment, while Noel's merger proposal to avoid an IPO will be defeated. The agenda also includes confirming the Sept 17 minutes.The Trusts argued that such moves would render their affirmative voting rights under Tata Sons Article 121 ineffective. Chandrasekaran is set to chair most of the resolutions, which would give him the casting vote in a tie. He will not chair the one on his own reappointment.The Trusts have therefore sought a declaration from the high court that the Sept 17 resolution on Chandrasekaran's reappointment is invalid, and a direction restraining Tata Sons from acting on it. Chandrasekaran’s current term expires on Feb 20, 2027. SDTT specifically seeks to restrain Chandrasekaran, Manwani or anyone else chairing a Tata Sons board meeting from exercising a casting vote when Trust-nominated directors differ.At the heart of the dispute are Articles 118 and 121 of Tata Sons' articles of association. The Trusts argue that Article 121 requires a majority of their nominee directors to vote in favour of key board resolutions. With only two nominees, that means both must support a resolution, and a casting vote cannot cure a 1-1 split. In their reading, the casting vote applies only when the whole board is tied.They also said Chandrasekaran's reappointment should have followed Article 118, which provides for a selection committee. To support the case, they cited section 10(1) of the Companies Act, which binds a company to its articles, and the Supreme Court's 2021 ruling in TCS v Cyrus Investments.Tata Sons, however, argues that Article 118 applies only to the appointment of a new chairman, and that Article 121 gives the chairman a casting vote when the votes of the two Trusts' nominees are divided.The Trusts said they decided to go to court because a series of communications to Tata Sons since Sept 17, raising objections and seeking corrective action, failed to elicit a satisfactory response.On Nov 25, the two Trusts, which together hold about 30% of Tata Sons, passed by majority resolutions backing legal action against the company and its entire board. Srinivasan and Vijay Singh voted against. Both are among the four trustees common to the two Trusts, alongside Noel and his son Neville Tata. Bhat is the other SDTT trustee, while Noel's daughter Maya Tata and Tushad Dubash are the other RDTT trustees.Of the Rs 65 crore claimed, SDTT seeks Rs 50 crore and RDTT Rs 15 crore from Tata Sons and five directors: Chandrasekaran, Srinivasan, Manwani, executive director and CFO Saurabh Agrawal, and independent director Anita George.
Article Summary: Chandra set to chair board for most resolutions, giving him casting vote in a tie. Trusts fear the same device will be used to push through resolutions including conversion of Tata Sons into a public company and its listing. Tata Sons argues that Article 118 applies only to the appointment of a new chairman, and that Article 121 gives the chairman a casting vote.

Article Title: Colombo Security Conclave reaffirms commitment to promote regional peace
Article Text:
Participating in the meeting, NSA Ajit Doval said India is committed to working closely with CSC nations to enhance collective capacities for dealing with the evolving serious security challenges.

NEW DELHI: The 8th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave in the Maldives reaffirmed the “collective commitment” of member states to promote regional peace and security through sustained cooperation, calling for strengthening collaboration across the five pillars of cooperation, particularly through training, sharing best practices and capacity-building initiatives.The five pillars of CSC cooperation are maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime, cyber security and protection of critical infrastructure and technology, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.Member-states including Maldives, India, Mauritius and Sri Lanka also adopted the Roadmap of Cooperation for 2026-27, setting out key deliverables and planned activities under the pillars. CSC was formed to promote closer cooperation on matters of security and to strengthen partnerships for enhancing regional security in the Indian Ocean Region. Bangladesh also participated in the event. Its membership was approved but Dhaka is still completing the internal processes necessary for membership requirements.Participating in the meeting, NSA Ajit Doval said India is committed to working closely with CSC nations to enhance collective capacities for dealing with the evolving serious security challenges.
Article Summary: The 8th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave in the Maldives reaffirmed the ‘collective commitment’ of member states to promote regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. The five pillars of CSC cooperation are maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime.

Article Title: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
Article Text:
SC bound the regulator to the time frame suggested by it, which was four months to follow the process under the 2006 Act and regulations.

Supreme Court: Every day’s delay allows unlabelled food to be sold

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has set a timeline to implement the front-of-package labelling for each nutrient of concern on packaged food.The top court granted four months’ time to food regulator FSSAI to frame rules, and one year’s time to make it compulsory for companies. The labels indicating high sugar, saturated fat and salt will be placed inside red, hexagonal shapes.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran pushed the regulator to fall in line and discharge its duty to protect the interest of consumers, noting that FSSAI showed “reluctance” on labelling followed in many countries to make consumers aware of the harmful contents.Supreme Court said India is facing a major public health crisis, driven in part by the consumption of foods high in saturated fat, sugar and/or salt. “The population’s exposure to harmful substances must be controlled, their consumption must be discouraged, and consumers must be protected from practices detrimental to health used by the food businesses. Preventive measures, that are most effective, must therefore be undertaken in an effort to respect, protect and guarantee the right to health,” the bench said, adding that it cannot remain a “mute spectator” in such a situation.Supreme Court bound the regulator to the time frame suggested by it, which was four months to follow the process under the 2006 Act and regulations. It agreed that food business operators be granted a year’s time from the date of notification to implement the labelling regime. The intervening 365 days will be a “voluntary implementation” period.“Every day of delay means that packaged foods continue to be sold without such labels, to the detriment of the rights to health, food and informed choice, respectively... FSSAI should anticipate potential impediments and take active measures to ensure that they are resolved or adequately addressed,” the bench said.“The right to health has expanded from being limited to healthcare to addressing the broader determinants of health and conditions congenial to good health; the right to food now requires access to food which is sufficient in terms of both quantity and quality; and the right to informed choice has expanded its focus towards confronting the broader informational and social order that people live in,” Supreme Court said.It rejected FSSAI’s plea that there be only one hexagon within which levels of ‘high sugar’, ‘high saturated fat’ and ‘high salt’ would be placed, directing there be a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern. “The font size... must be such that it remains clear, prominent and readily legible alongside pictograms,” Supreme Court added.
Article Summary: Supreme Court bound the regulator to the time frame suggested by it, which was four months to follow the process under the 2006 Act and regulations. It agreed that food business operators be granted a year’s time from the date of notification to implement the labelling regime.

Article Title: India-Germany submarine partnership can act as a catalyst for Indo-Pacific security: German envoy
Article Text:
Wieck said the project will see extensive transfer of technology in the underwater domain, not just limited to the submarines, as he highlighted overarching policy frameworks established by Berlin to guarantee reliability.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With the India-Germany Project-75 India (P-75I) conventional submarine deal in CCS for final approval, Germany has reiterated its commitment to delivering comprehensive technology transfer under the long-term industrial partnership with India. German ambassador to India Jasper Wieck told TOI in an interview mutual trust regarding protection of sensitive technologies will be key to this partnership.Pegged at $ 8-9 billion, the proposed P-75I deal involving Germany’s TKMS and India’s Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) to build 6 submarines equipped with the vital Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) technology—which allows vessels to remain submerged for weeks without surfacing—will be one of the largest-ever defence contracts signed by India.Wieck said the project will see extensive transfer of technology in the underwater domain, not just limited to the submarines, as he highlighted overarching policy frameworks established by Berlin to guarantee reliability."Germany has committed to becoming a reliable defence-industrial partner of India. The bilateral defense industrial cooperation roadmap, which was signed in April this year, explicitly includes defense technology transfer," said Wieck.Asked about compartmentalisation and protection of sensitive submarine technology transferred to India, Wieck said technologies related to P-75I will only be shared with related Indian companies and government bodies. "Now, ultimately sharing technology with partners is always a question of trust and reliability, but here I can confirm India and Germany are definitely trusted partners in both directions," Wieck said.Speaking alongside Wieck about the technical execution of the project, TKMS global CEO Oliver Burkhard said P-75I is built around the transfer of the design of the submarine which will belong to the Indian Navy."You can't run a submarine if you haven't understood it. A few core technologies are protected in every partnership but India will get full access to that what they need to run, maintain, sustain those boats over the next 40 years," said Burkhard.Addressing India's concerns regarding TKMS' historical submarine contracts with Turkey, Burkhard clarified that each international program is strictly isolated and governed by German sovereign oversight."India does not have to worry because every program is ring-fenced. The technology, data, and intellectual property stay in that country and is protected by agreements between the two governments. The design India will receive is a highly advanced, unique-to-India boat and that has nothing to do with Turkey anymore," Burkhard said.Ambassador Wieck highlighted how the submarine agreement fits into Germany’s broader Indo-Pacific strategy, considering particularly regional security challenges and efforts to maintain rules-based maritime order."India plays a central role in the Indo-Pacific and India and Germany have a shared interest in upholding and defending the rules-based international order. And in the Indo-Pacific, that means the freedom of navigation and the security of lifelines of communication across the oceans. P75I is a long-term engagement with the potential of becoming a catalyst for deepening security and safety in the Indian Ocean," noted Wieck.Asked if India's ties with Russia might limit Germany's willingness to transfer sensitive naval technology, Wieck stressed mutual respect for sovereign choices."Each and every country around the world has its own network of partners and friends across the globe...instead of dwelling on India's partnerships with other countries, I'd rather focus on broadening and deepening the Indo-German partnership. Mutual trust, also regarding the protection of sensitive defense technology, is of course the key to that partnership," said Wieck.According to Burkhard, the submarine partnership might offer an opportunity for turning India a hub for Southeast Asian nations or others who want to join the submarine programme. "Submarines of the future can be built for other nations with, for example, a German design on one side, and on the other Indian competencies when it comes to assembly and manufacturing. A number of countries are approaching us. We are the global leaders in conventional submarines. ..so, if you can offer, for example, a country which is interested and it goes along with the political interests of India and Germany also to be part of a submarine building programme...it can be steered from a new hub in Asia, which will then be India for us," he said.On the need to adhere to strict delivery schedules, Burkhard emphasised TKMS’ delivery track record - citing four submarines and one frigate delivered this year - and noted that execution is a shared responsibility with MDL, with indigenous content reaching 70% on the final boat. While acknowledging past delays, he stressed confidence in meeting timelines, stating, "we are also in a delivery mode which shows hopefully some confidence that, of course, we will meet the timelines".Addressing concerns over integrating the AIP system into a new design for India’s P75I submarines, Burkhard called AIP a proven technology operated by the German Navy for over 20 years and across more than 50 submarines in service or under contract. He noted that India will own the design for P75I, making future modifications easier without having to depend on the foreign original equipment manufacturer.
Article Summary: The India-Germany Project-75 India (P-75I) conventional submarine deal is in CCS for final approval. Germany has reiterated its commitment to delivering comprehensive technology transfer under the long-term industrial partnership with India. Pegged at $ 8-9 billion, the proposed deal involves Germany’s TKMS and India’S Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) to build 6 submarines.

Article Title: Road ministry tightens bidding norms to keep poor performers out of fully govt-funded projects
Article Text:
The revised framework also does away with sequential counter-offers to the second and third lowest bidders. If the lowest bidder is found ineligible, the authority can annul the bidding process and invite fresh bids.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The road transport ministry has linked contractors’ bidding capacity to their performance ratings and delays in ongoing projects, replacing the earlier practice of assessing their best-performing financial year for fully government-funded or EPC projects.These changes in the bidding and contract conditions have been made to address concerns over the quality of construction and delays in project execution. The modifications in the Request for Proposal (RFP) for Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) contracts, which replaced the existing framework issued in March 2019, seek to make the contractor selection process more performance-oriented. This will prevent contractors with a poor execution record from taking on additional projects beyond their capacity.The revised framework also does away with sequential counter-offers to the second and third lowest bidders. If the lowest bidder is found ineligible, the authority can annul the bidding process and invite fresh bids.Further, the ministry has brought in stricter norms for joint ventures (JVs), reducing the maximum number of members from three to two. JVs will generally be allowed only for projects costing more than Rs 1,000 crore, with enhanced minimum participation requirements for the other member.Technical eligibility conditions have also been strengthened, particularly for major bridges, structures and tunnels, to ensure that contractors bidding for specialised infrastructure projects have relevant experience.The modified RFP links performance security to contractors’ ratings, with the requirement ranging from 3% to 5% of the bid price. It also provides for electronic submission of security instruments.Further, the ministry has rationalised the number of non-performance criteria from 20 to seven, with clearly defined thresholds and assessment periods. Provisions dealing with catastrophic failures, termination of projects, debarment and insolvency have also been strengthened.To improve transparency, bidders will have to disclose details of ongoing disputes, litigation, arbitration and penal actions and keep such information updated during the bidding process.
Article Summary: The road transport ministry has linked contractors’ bidding capacity to their performance ratings and delays in ongoing projects. The revised framework also does away with sequential counter-offers to the second and third lowest bidders. If the lowest bidder is found ineligible, the authority can annul the bidding process and invite fresh bids.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Govt on Thursday asked industry to stop diverting highly subsidised agricultural-grade urea for industrial use and to cut costs, pointing out that while farm-grade urea costs just Rs 6 per kg, industrial-grade urea is at least 10 times more expensive. Diversion of urea for non-agricultural use has been a major concern for govt as India remains dependent on import of urea to meet domestic requirements.Speaking at an event of Fertiliser Association of India (FAI), fertiliser secretary Rajat Kumar Mishra said over eight crore farmers out of which 87% have small and marginal landholdings get subsidised fertilisers at only Rs 6 per kg for urea and technical-grade urea costs Rs 60–Rs 70 per kg. “Please help to stop the diversion of fertiliser from agriculture to industry. It is actually happening, and happening in a big way,” he said.Mishra also urged manufacturers and importers to reduce production costs without compromising quality, as the current level of govt subsidy is not sustainable. He also expressed concern over “tagging” of highly-subsidised urea with other fertilisers by their dealers while selling products to farmers.The department had earlier asked states to ensure installation of GPS tracking on all vehicles transporting fertilisers from ports and railways to the companies, to ensure that highly subsidised fertiliser — urea, diammonium phosphate (DAP), nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK), and potash — are not diverted for industrial use.Senior FAI office-bearer said on Thursday that govt should boost domestic production of fertiliser and diversify the source of raw material to reduce the challenges and supply disruptions because of crisis such as the West Asia conflict. “We must recognise that India’s fertiliser ecosystem continues to remain vulnerable to external shocks,” FAI chairperson S Sankarasubramanian said.
Article Summary: The government has called on the industry to cease the diversion of subsidised farm-grade urea for industrial purposes. Diversion of Urea for non-agricultural use has been a major concern for govt. India remains dependent on import of urea to meet domestic requirements.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
