NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Kolkata man buys 2 plates of chicken momos for Rs 109 each, is charged Rs 10 extra for takeaway packaging; consumer commission orders outlet to refund fee, pay Rs 100 compensation, Rs 2,000 legal cost
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





KOLKATA: A Kolkata food outlet has been asked to pay Rs 50,000 to a consumer commission's legal aid fund for charging a customer Rs 10 to pack two plates of chicken momos, with the commission ruling that takeaway packaging is the seller's responsibility. The customer had bought two plates of chicken momos, each priced at Rs 109, from the outlet on October 29, 2024. The additional Rs 10 on the bill for packaging led to a dispute after the customer sought a refund of the amount, which the outlet declined to provide.The customer then approached the consumer commission, seeking relief over the charge. In its defence, the company claimed the customer had asked for extra packaging because he was travelling on a motorcycle and wanted to avoid spillage while keeping the food safe and hygienic. It said the fee had been disclosed in advance and that the customer had accepted it before placing the order.The commission, however, found no material on record to support the company's version. It said the outlet could not establish either that the customer had requested the packaging or that he had been told about the additional charge beforehand. The bench of president Manoj Kumar Rai and member Gopal Chandra Roy relied on Section 36(5) of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, which places the cost of making goods fit for delivery on the seller, unless there is an agreement to the contrary.The commission said the outlet was therefore required to pack the food for takeaway at its own expense. Charging the customer for this service, without proving that he had specifically sought it or agreed to pay for it, amounted to deficiency in service.The outlet has been directed to return the Rs 10 packaging fee and pay Rs 100 as compensation to the customer, besides Rs 2,000 towards litigation costs. In addition, the commission ordered the company to deposit Rs 50,000 into its Consumer Legal Aid Account.
Article Summary: A Kolkata food outlet has been asked to pay Rs 50,000 to a consumer commission's legal aid fund. The customer had bought two plates of chicken momos, each priced at Rs 109. The additional Rs 10 on the bill for packaging led to a dispute after the customer sought a refund.

Article Title: RBI continues to bring back gold to India as it repatriates 60 tonnes more of yellow metal, India now houses 84% of its 880.52 metric tonnes gold reserves while remaining are with Bank of England and
Article Text:
Global gold prices fell by around 9%, with the average price dropping from $4,721 per troy ounce in April 2026 to $4,319 in September. (Image for representative purpose only)

RBI moves back most of India’s gold reserves

India’s forex reserves

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been bringing back India’s gold stored abroad for some time now and it continued to shift the yellow metal reserves back even in this year.However, what is interesting to note is that gold accounted for a smaller proportion of the country's overall foreign exchange reserves at the end of September, data released on Wednesday showed.Despite the increase in gold held within India, its share in total foreign exchange reserves fell to 14.38% at the end of September, compared with 16.7% six months earlier.According to the RBI's latest half-yearly report, India's gold reserves stood at 880.52 metric tonnes at the end of September. Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, equivalent to 84% of the total, were held within the country.The remaining 140.39 metric tonnes were kept with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements.RBI repatriated around 60 tonnes of gold during April-September 2026. India has been progressively repatriating its gold holdings over the past two years amid rising geopolitical risks. In March, 77% of the country's gold reserves were held domestically.India's foreign exchange reserves totalled $705.3 billion, according to the latest data released by the central bank on Friday.When reserves stood at $668.6 billion at the end of June, they were sufficient to cover 9.8 months of imports, the RBI said.The ratio of short-term debt to foreign exchange reserves climbed to 23% at the end of June 2026, up from 21.6% at the end of March. The ratio of volatile capital flows, including portfolio investments, to reserves also increased, reaching 68% at the end of June against 66.6% three months earlier.Most of India's foreign exchange reserves continue to be invested in securities issued by overseas governments. In addition, $35.95 billion was held as deposits with other central banks and the Bank for International Settlements, while $42.75 billion was deposited with commercial banks abroad."With the objective of exploring new strategies and products in reserve management while diversifying the portfolio, a small portion of the reserves is being managed by external asset managers," the RBI said.The period was marked by heightened geopolitical uncertainty, driven by the conflict in West Asia, interruptions to energy supplies and tighter monetary policies adopted by several major central banks.Global gold prices fell by around 9%, with the average price dropping from $4,721 per troy ounce in April 2026 to $4,319 in September."Prices responded to rising US Treasury yields, a stronger US dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy. The decline occurred despite continued investor demand for gold as a safe-haven and for portfolio diversification," the report noted.India's overall foreign exchange reserves, meanwhile, grew by $46.67 billion during April-September 2026. They increased from $691.11 billion at the end of March to $737.78 billion at the end of September.Of the $608.26 billion in foreign currency assets held at the end of September, $529.57 billion was invested in securities. A further $35.95 billion was placed with other central banks and the BIS, while $42.75 billion was maintained as deposits with commercial banks overseas.The report also pointed to shifts in the composition of global foreign exchange reserves. The US dollar's share fell from 57.18% in the first quarter of 2026 to 56.70% in the second quarter. Over the same period, the euro's share rose from 20.04% to 20.60%.The RBI reiterated that protecting the safety of India's foreign exchange reserves and ensuring their liquidity remain the central priorities in managing the portfolio, with returns optimised within these parameters.
Article Summary: India's gold reserves stood at 880.52 metric tonnes at the end of September. Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, equivalent to 84% of the total, were held within the country. The remaining 140.39 metric tonnes were kept with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements.

Article Title: Kolkata-bound flight fares for late December surge 30.2% in a week, led by Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad, while Delhi and Ahmedabad prices remain largely unchanged
Article Text:
Late-December airfares into Kolkata increased by a median of 30.2% in a single week (AI-generated image used for representative purposes)

In one week, the price of a late-December flight into Kolkata rose 30%. Across the rest of the network it moved 2.4.

A one-week move that only hit one city

Airfares to Kolkata surged across routes in a week, with Bengaluru seeing the steepest increase at 47.5%

One-week change in the fare for late-December travel, flights into Kolkata

The pattern points south

Why this is worth watching rather than concluding

What it means for you

The Short Version

About This Data

TOI-DPA Airline Price Index is a joint initiative of The Times of India and Decimal Point Analytics.

Source: Decimal Point Analytics Airline Price Index





Our tracker records the fare for travel 30 days ahead every day, which means it is currently pricing the last week of December.Between the week of 11 November and the week of 18 November, those late-December fares into Kolkata jumped by a median 30.2%.Across all 54 routes the same comparison gives 2.4%. This is one city, in one direction, in one week.Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and Pune lead the list. Delhi and Ahmedabad barely moved.That is the southern and western working population, not the northern one. It is also the same set of cities that drove the Durga Puja and Chhath surges earlier this autumn, which suggests the same travelling group booking a third trip.Late December in Kolkata covers Christmas, the year-end week and the start of the winter season, when the city is at its most pleasant and its social calendar is fullest.A single week of movement is a signal, not a finding. Fares at 30 days out move for reasons that have nothing to do with demand, including a carrier adjusting inventory or withdrawing a cheap bucket.What makes this one notable is how narrow it is. A pricing change usually shows up across a carrier's network.This shows up on one destination, from five origins, in one direction, in one week.If you are planning Kolkata over the year-end from Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune or Mumbai, the cheap window has probably already closed.Delhi and Ahmedabad have not moved, so those two origins are still priced as they were a fortnight ago.Late-December fares into Kolkata rose a median 30.2% in a single week. The rest of the network moved 2.4%.Bengaluru to Kolkata went from Rs 8,280 to Rs 12,214, a rise of 47.5%. Chennai rose 35.0% and Hyderabad 34.5.Delhi and Ahmedabad barely moved, so the surge is coming from the south and west.One week of movement is a signal rather than a conclusion, but it is unusually narrow: one city, one direction, five origins.Figures compare the fare quoted 30 days before departure in the week to 24 November against the same measure a week earlier, which means travel dates in the last week of December.The Airline Fare Tracker records the median fare shown on Google Flights for 54 routes between Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune. Fares are captured every day, and this analysis covers 211 consecutive days from 28 April to 24 November 2026 with no missing dates.The index sets every route to 100 on 28 April and weights routes by monthly scheduled seats.Limits. These are advertised medians, not fares finally paid. All eight cities are metros, so smaller routes are not measured. There is no year-earlier comparison yet, so changes across the period cannot be separated from seasonal demand or from the fuel-driven capacity reduction that sits inside it.Roughly 6% of daily readings were filled in by the data provider where a capture failed. The tracker records which airline flies a route but not which airline charged a given fare.
Article Summary: Late-December airfares into Kolkata increased by a median of 30.2% in a single week. Bengaluru saw the steepest increase at 47.5%. Chennai rose 35.0% and Hyderabad 34.5. Delhi and Ahmedabad barely moved, so the surge is coming from the south.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio mansion carries a $120,000 tax bill, with $72,000 potentially benefiting local schools
Article Text:
Travis Kelce mansion (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce's Ohio mansion could generate $120,000 in annual property taxes

Travis Kelce's mansion could bring an unexpected boost to Cleveland schools

This creates an interesting link between the property and the educational system serving the wider community.The estimated $72,000 allocation is not a personal donation from Kelce or a charitable contribution announced by the football star. Rather, it represents a potential public funding contribution through property taxation.For Kelce, whose career has brought him considerable financial success, the Ohio estate represents a connection to the place where his story began. Article Title: Bengaluru man pays Rs 2 lakh to book residential plot, cancels deal over missing legal documents; builder fails to refund despite written assurance, consumer commission orders Rs 2 lakh refund with 9%
Article Text:
(AI image) A Bengaluru consumer commission directed a real estate company to refund Rs 2 lakh to a man.





BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed a real estate company and its two directors to refund Rs 2 lakh to a 41-year-old man who cancelled the booking of a residential plot after the builder allegedly failed to provide essential property documents. The commission also ordered them to pay Rs 25,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban), in an order dated October 7, directed Virtue Infra Builders Pvt Ltd and its directors, R M Harikrishna and Aravinda Kumar, to refund the booking amount with 9% annual interest from July 19, 2024, until payment.The commission also ordered the opposite parties to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service, Rs 10,000 for pain and suffering, and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. They have been given 45 days to comply with the order.According to the complaint filed by Muni Rao, he had approached the company to purchase a residential plot in its Virtue Star City project at Mathkur village in Bengaluru North. Based on the company's representations about the property's title, approvals and availability for immediate registration, he agreed to purchase plot No. 66, measuring 1,410 sq ft.On July 19, 2024, Rao paid Rs 2 lakh as advance booking amount, comprising Rs 1.5 lakh through cheque and Rs 50,000 through an online transaction.However, after receiving the payment, the company allegedly failed to provide the complete legal documents required to verify the title and legality of the transaction. These included mother deeds and title documents, land conversion order, approved layout plan, RERA approval and e-Khata documents.Unable to verify the property's legal status, Rao decided to cancel the booking and sought a refund. Despite repeated requests, phone calls and emails, the company did not return the money, according to the complaint.On August 21, 2024, the company acknowledged its liability to refund the booking amount through an email and assured Rao that the money would be credited by November 20, 2024. It also apologised for the delay and assured him that the refund would be processed. However, the payment was not made even after the promised deadline, forcing him to approach the consumer commission.The commission noted that the builder and its directors failed to appear before it despite receiving notice and did not file their written version. The matter was consequently heard ex parte.After examining the complainant's affidavit and supporting documents, the commission observed that the company had failed to furnish the necessary property documents despite receiving the advance amount. It also noted that the company had acknowledged its liability to refund the money but had failed to honour its assurance.The commission held the company and its two directors jointly and severally liable, observing that the complainant was neither given possession of the plot nor refunded the deposited amount. It concluded that their conduct amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.
Article Summary: Bengaluru consumer commission directed a real estate company to refund Rs 2 lakh to a man. The 41-year-old cancelled the booking of a residential plot after the builder allegedly failed to provide essential property documents. The commission also ordered them to pay Rs 25,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses.

Article Title: Bengaluru man relocates from Chennai, pays Voltas Rs 1,770 to reinstall AC, technicians damage it during reinstallation, consumer commission orders Voltas to pay Rs 33,770 compensation
Article Text:
A Bengaluru consumer commission ruled that Voltas Ltd must compensate a customer for air conditioner damage.





BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay Rs 33,770 to a customer after finding deficiency in service by its technicians, who allegedly damaged his air conditioner while reinstalling it after he relocated from Chennai. The company has since paid the compensation amount to the customer.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban) directed the company to pay Rs 25,000 as consolidated compensation for the damage and operational loss of the AC, along with 3% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint.It also ordered a refund of Rs 1,770 towards installation charges, Rs 5,000 for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 2,000 towards litigation expenses.According to the complaint filed by S Balaji, 37, his Voltas 1.5-tonne split AC (Model 183SY) was in working condition when it was dismantled in Chennai in March 2025. A technical fitness report issued by Dynamic Cool Center had certified that the unit was functional before it was moved to Bengaluru.After relocating, Balaji approached Voltas for reinstallation on April 19, 2025, and paid Rs 1,770 for the service. He alleged that the technicians deployed by the company lacked the necessary expertise and leaked the entire refrigerant gas charge during the installation process, leaving the machine non-functional.The complaint stated that Voltas technicians returned on May 1 and refilled the refrigerant gas without charging him. However, Balaji alleged that they left the cooling system unpressurised and exposed, allowing atmospheric moisture to enter over the next 12 days. This allegedly damaged the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and fan motor.Despite raising multiple service requests and escalating the matter through emails, the AC developed recurring reset problems and eventually stopped functioning completely. Balaji also approached the National Consumer Helpline, but his grievances were marked as disposed of without a technical resolution.The commission noted that the complainant had submitted documents establishing that the AC was functional before its relocation and that it developed major defects following the reinstallation carried out by Voltas. It also observed that the company had failed to provide any contrary technical evidence or written explanation."The deployment of untrained staff and the subsequent terminal damage to the machine amounts to a deficiency of service," the commission observed.However, it declined to award the full original purchase value of Rs 33,000 sought by Balaji, noting that the AC was not brand new when it was reinstalled in Bengaluru and had already been used in Chennai. It said awarding the full purchase value without accounting for depreciation would be inequitable.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, passed the order on September 30, 2026. Voltas and its Bengaluru branch manager did not appear before the commission despite service of notice and were proceeded against ex parte.
Article Summary: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay Rs 33,770 to a customer. Voltas technicians allegedly damaged his air conditioner while reinstalling it after he relocated from Chennai. The company has since paid the compensation amount to the customer.

Article Title: Bengaluru woman’s Rs 12.7 lakh Groww portfolio falls to Rs 84,508 after tech glitch during Rs 10 lakh withdrawal; firm told to refund Rs 11.85 lakh with 6% interest and pay Rs 12,000
Article Text:
(Representative) Ranjana Priya's investment of Rs 8.12 lakhs in the Groww app initially flourished, reaching Rs 12.7 lakhs





BENGALURU: Imagine watching your savings grow to over Rs 12 lakh on an investment app, only to see the balance shrink to under Rs 1 lakh the moment you try to withdraw your own money. That is what a city woman faced when the Groww app displayed a sudden, unexplained error after she sought a redemption. The Bengaluru (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held the platform liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The saga began when Ranjana Priya, a resident of HSR Layout, Sector 2, trusted the platform's market reputation and assurances and invested a total of Rs 8.12 lakhs through systematic investment plans (SIPs) on the Groww app. Favourable market performance pushed her portfolio up significantly, and the official dashboard showed its valuation had reached Rs 12,70,404 as of November 26, 2025.Citing urgent personal and financial requirements, she placed a digital request for a partial redemption of Rs 10 lakh. What followed, she said, were "alarming errors". The dashboard updated to show her total invested amount as just Rs 84,508, wiping out the rest of her portfolio value.Priya said she ran from pillar to post, raising support tickets by phone and email and complaining to SEBI on November 27. Nothing was resolved.On November 30, Groww credited a mere Rs 15,500 to her bank account. By her reconciliation, her total investment value stood at Rs 12.70 lakhs. After accounting for the amount redeemed, Rs 11.85 lakhs was left unaccounted for.She then raised statutory grievances on the e-Jagriti platform through WhatsApp four times between December 7 and December 25, 2025. The opposite parties neither corrected their financial records nor refunded the balance. Leaving her with no option, Priya approached the commission on April 22, 2026, and sought a refund for mental agony, harassment and financial hardship.She named Groww Invest Tech Pvt Ltd and Nextbillion Technology Pvt Ltd (Groww)/Billionbrains Garage Ventures Pvt Ltd. Both appeared through counsel but did not file their written version within the statutory 45 days. Their version was taken as not filed, in line with a judgment of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, and despite sufficient opportunities, they never mounted a defence.After going through the records and hearing arguments, the commission observed that her allegations stood unchallenged as the firms had forfeited their right to defence. It accepted as true her digital records, including the portfolio value of Rs 12.7 lakhs and the redemption request for Rs 10 lakh. The platform's act of reducing the visible portfolio value to Rs 84,508, coupled with its complete failure to respond to four separate institutional warnings from the National Grievance Helpline, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, it said. It termed the withholding of Rs 11.85 lakhs belonging to a retail investor "completely unauthorised, illegal and high handed".The commission added that a digital investment platform cannot hold a consumer's hard-earned savings hostage under the guise of an unrectified technical glitch or internal database error. The documents showed beyond doubt that of her Rs 12. 7 lakhs portfolio, Rs 11.85 lakhs remained unaccounted for and was withheld without valid legal justification, causing mental agony and financial distress to a complainant dependent on her savings.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra MS and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani directed both firms, jointly and severally, to refund Rs 11,85,896 with 6% annual interest from the date of redemption until actual realisation. It further ordered them to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service and mental harassment and Rs 2,000 as litigation costs.Meanwhile, Groww stated that it will be filing an appeal before the Karnataka State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission and place complete records before it.In a statement, Groww explained: "During the course of 2024 and 2025, the customer redeemed units in several schemes through the Groww app. All of these redemptions were processed, and the money was paid to her registered bank account directly by the clearing corporation. Because of an error in display of holdings, her portfolio dashboard did not fully reflect some of these redemptions. It continued to show units she had already redeemed, valued at current market prices, and so showed her portfolio as worth about Rs 12.7 lakh which the customer tried to redeem. ""The dashboard was thereafter corrected. The corrected value of her holdings i.e., Rs 84,508 matched what she actually held after the redemptions had gone through. The amount claimed in the report as withheld is approx Rs 11.85 lakh which is the incorrectly displayed portfolio value (Rs 12.70 lakh) minus the corrected figure (Rs 84,508). When the customer reached out to us after placing her redemption requests, our team spoke with her over the phone and explained that the dashboard had been showing incorrect values, which had since been corrected. On December 1, 2025, our escalation team followed up in writing, confirming that the dashboard now reflected her accurate holdings and sharing a scheme-wise breakdown of her current investments. We also encouraged her to verify these details against her CAMS statement, which shows every purchase and redemption in her account, and offered further assistance if she needed it.”
Article Summary: Ranjana Priya's investment of Rs 8.12 lakhs in the Groww app initially flourished, reaching Rs 12.7 lakhs. She placed a digital request for a partial redemption of Rs 10 lakh. What followed, she said, were "alarming errors" The dashboard updated to show her total invested amount as just Rs 84,508.

Article Title: For 20 years, a national highway blocked Varanasi airport's runway expansion; now, in a first for India, a 2.89-km underpass is being built to let aircraft fly above it
Article Text:
Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport is set to undergo significant expansion. A 2.89-km underpass will allow the highway to run beneath the extended runway.

The underpass is designed to ensure that highway traffic can continue moving beneath the expanded runway rather than being diverted or interrupted by airport operations.

Nearly 60% of the underpass work had been completed by November 2026, while the new terminal building had reached 71% completion.

A plan that remained on paper for two decades

The Airports Authority of India (AAI) had proposed extending the airport's runway in its 2004 masterplan

The airport's annual passenger-handling capacity is expected to rise from 39 lakh to around 99 lakh.

Fog exposed the cost of a short runway

The Airports Authority of India has taken assistance from experts at IIT Delhi for the tunnel's design

How the project will change the airport

Keeping road traffic moving while the airport grows

(With inputs from Rajeev Dikshit)





VARANASI: For nearly two decades, the expansion of Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi remained caught in an unusual geographical predicament.A railway line ran along its eastern side, while the Varanasi-Lucknow national highway lay to its west. Extending the runway was essential to accommodate larger aircraft, but doing so meant confronting a question that had no conventional answer: How could the airport expand without disrupting a major highway?The solution was to take the highway underground.Varanasi is now building a 2.89-km underpass on NH-31, allowing the airport's expanded runway to pass above it.Once completed, the project will make it the first airport in India to have a national highway running beneath its runway. The underpass, being constructed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), is estimated to cost Rs 649.44 crore, while the larger airport expansion project is worth around Rs 2,870 crore.Nearly 60% of the underpass work had been completed by November 2026, while the new terminal building had reached 71% completion. The underpass is targeted for completion by March 2027, while the terminal is expected to be ready by July 2027.The project is not merely about building a tunnel beneath an airport. It is an attempt to resolve a long-standing infrastructure conflict involving two transport networks that had left little room for the airport to grow.The Airports Authority of India (AAI) had proposed extending the airport's runway in its 2004 masterplan. The existing runway, measuring around 2,750 metres, was considered inadequate for the airport's long-term ambitions, particularly its ability to handle larger passenger aircraft and cargo planes.The proposal envisaged extending the runway to 4,075 metres. But the geographical constraints proved difficult to overcome.With a railway track on the eastern side, the airport's expansion could only take place towards the west, where the Varanasi-Lucknow highway was located. Extending the runway in that direction meant that the highway's existing alignment would have to be preserved even as the airport expanded above it.The AAI approached the Uttar Pradesh government in March 2015, seeking the land required for the expansion. The proposal gained momentum in 2017 when the authority restarted the process of identifying land.In 2018, the AAI approved a plan to extend the runway over the highway while providing an underpass for vehicular movement. The proposal also offered a solution to the long-pending alignment issue on the highway, which was being upgraded."It will be India's first highway to pass under the runway of an airport. The proposed underpass will also solve the long-pending issue of deciding the alignment of NH-56, which is being converted into a four-lane road," NHAI project director (Varanasi) S B Singh told TOI in 2018.Despite the approval, the project did not move at the pace envisaged. Land acquisition requirements and other administrative and technical issues continued to hold it up.The urgency of expanding the airport became more apparent in January 2023, when poor visibility disrupted flight operations.On the night of January 8, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath's departure from Varanasi was cancelled after dense fog prevented his flight from taking off. He had to return to the circuit house for the night. The following day, he was also made to wait at the airport for visibility to improve.During his visit, the CM sought an explanation for the difficulties faced by the airport during extreme weather conditions.Officials informed him that the airport had an Instrument Landing System (ILS) of Category I, whereas Category III systems permit aircraft to land in much lower visibility conditions. A longer runway was also part of the airport's infrastructure requirements.Adityanath subsequently directed officials to expedite the runway expansion process.In July 2023, the district administration sought Rs 1,030 crore from the state government's civil aviation department for acquiring land across seven villages. The AAI's original requirement had included 593.77 acres in Mangari, Bikunthpur, Karmi, Ghamhapur Karmi, Sagunaha and Pura Raghunathpur.The Union Cabinet cleared the larger airport expansion proposal in June 2024, and the foundation stone for the airport development project was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 20, 2024.The separate underpass project subsequently received its own push. Modi laid the foundation for the 2.89-km tunnel in April 2025.The underpass is only one part of a comprehensive expansion plan aimed at more than doubling the airport's passenger-handling capacity.The runway will be extended from around 2,745 metres to 4,075 metres, allowing the airport to handle larger aircraft. The airport's annual passenger-handling capacity is expected to rise from 39 lakh to around 99 lakh.The expansion also includes a new terminal building, an extended apron, a parallel taxiway and other associated infrastructure.The new terminal will have an area of around 99,500 square metres, compared with the existing 24,500 square metres. The number of aircraft parking bays will increase from 11 to 20, while peak-hour passenger-handling capacity will rise from 1,050 to around 6,050.The new terminal is also being designed to reflect Varanasi's cultural identity. Its architectural elements draw inspiration from the trident of Lord Shiva, the Kashi Vishwanath Dham and the jharokhas of Rajasthan's palaces. Its interiors will feature representations of Nataraja's mudras, the ghats along the Ganga, boats and local handicrafts.The airport's expanded area will cover 774 acres, including 639 acres inside and 135 acres outside the airport premises.The underpass is designed to ensure that highway traffic can continue moving beneath the expanded runway rather than being diverted or interrupted by airport operations.The Airports Authority of India has taken assistance from experts at IIT Delhi for the tunnel's design. Safety arrangements outlined for the project include round-the-clock video surveillance, route-patrolling vehicles and ambulances for emergency assistance. CRPF personnel are also to be deployed on both sides of the tunnel.The construction requires coordination between the AAI, NHAI, the district administration and the executing agencies, given that the runway and highway infrastructure are being developed as part of the same expansion plan.During an inspection on November 21, divisional commissioner K Vijayendra Pandian reviewed the progress of the terminal and underpass projects. He directed officials to accelerate construction while maintaining quality standards and ensuring that the work was completed within the stipulated deadlines.With nearly 60% of the underpass construction complete, the March 2027 deadline is now the next major milestone.For Varanasi, the project represents the resolution of a planning dilemma that had persisted since the airport's expansion was first proposed. Rather than forcing the airport and highway to compete for the same stretch of land, the solution has been to place one transport corridor beneath the other.The result will be an airport runway extended over a national highway, allowing aircraft and road traffic to use the same geographical space without sharing the same level.
Article Summary: Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport is set to undergo significant expansion. A 2.89-km underpass will allow the highway to run beneath the extended runway. The airport's annual passenger-handling capacity is expected to rise from 39 lakh to around 99 lakh.

Article Title: Gurgaon man buys Rs 1.73 lakh LG refrigerator, faces five compressor failures, consumer commission orders replacement and Rs 61,000 payout
Article Text:
Consumer faced persistent failures with their LG refrigerator and sought resolution through a commission.

Key Highlights

A Gurgaon consumer commission ordered LG Electronics India, its service centre and Vijay Sales to replace a refrigerator bought for Rs 1.73 lakh after its compressor allegedly failed five times.

The commission awarded Rs 50,000 in compensation for mental harassment and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses to the complainant, Lokesh Mehta.

The refrigerator's compressor reportedly began malfunctioning within two months of purchase, despite repeated repair attempts and a protection plan valid till October 2027.

The companies were proceeded against ex-parte after failing to appear before the commission and have been directed to comply within 45 days, failing which 12% annual interest will apply.





GURGAON: A premium refrigerator bought for Rs 1.73 lakh allegedly developed repeated compressor failures, with the component breaking down five times, forcing its owner to approach a consumer commission. The commission has now ordered the refrigerator to be replaced with a new unit and directed the companies involved to pay Rs 61,000 in compensation and litigation expenses.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gurgaon, held LG Electronics India, its service centre and retailer Vijay Sales guilty of deficiency in service after they failed to appear before it and contest the complaint.The commission directed the companies to replace the LG refrigerator, model GC-X257CQES, with a new unit of the same model. It also awarded Rs 50,000 to complainant Lokesh Mehta for mental harassment, pain and agony, besides Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.Mehta had purchased the refrigerator for Rs 1,73,480 and alleged that its compressor began malfunctioning within two months of the purchase. According to the service records submitted before the commission, the compressor failed five times. The consumer alleged that the appliance was a defective product and that repeated repair attempts failed to resolve the problem.The refrigerator was also covered under a protection plan valid till October 2027, but the repeated breakdowns allegedly continued to trouble the buyer. After failing to get a replacement and compensation from the companies, Mehta sent them a legal notice in March 2026. When his demand did not yield a response, he approached the consumer commission.The commission noted that the opposite parties had been duly served but did not appear before it. They were proceeded against ex-parte.Mehta submitted his affidavit along with supporting documents, including the purchase invoice, warranty and protection-plan documents, email correspondence, service-related records, grievance details, text messages and the legal notice.The commission comprising president Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur. Member Jyoti Siwach in its order said the documents placed on record corroborated the complainant’s version. It observed that there was nothing to disbelieve or discredit his evidence.“Since the OPs in this case have been proceeded against ex-parte and there is no evidence on their behalf on the record of this file,” the commission noted, the complainant’s evidence remained unrebutted and there was no reason to disbelieve it.The commission held the companies guilty of deficiency in service and allowed the complaint.The companies have been directed to pay the awarded amount within 45 days of the order. If they fail to comply, the amount will attract interest at 12% per annum till its realisation.The commission further said that failure to comply with the order could lead to execution proceedings under Section 71(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The companies could also face prosecution under Section 72, which provides for imprisonment of one month to three years, a fine ranging from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh, or both.
Article Summary: Gurgaon consumer commission ordered LG Electronics India, its service centre and Vijay Sales to replace a refrigerator bought for Rs 1.73 lakh after its compressor allegedly failed five times. Commission awarded Rs 50,000 in compensation for mental harassment and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses to the complainant, Lokesh Mehta.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu rain alert: IMD warns of heavy rain in Theni Ghat areas, thunderstorms across state till Saturday as northeast monsoon revives after weeks of deficit
Article Text:
Heavy rain is expected in the Ghat areas of Theni district, along with continued thunderstorms across Tamil Nadu

Reservoirs receive fresh inflows

Chennai unlikely to get significant rain





CHENNAI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rain in the Ghat areas of Theni district on Friday, while thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to continue across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal until Saturday.The warning comes as the northeast monsoon regained strength over southern Tamil Nadu on Thursday after weeks of inadequate rainfall, bringing heavy showers to coastal districts, flooding roads and school premises and forcing restrictions at popular waterfalls.Kayalpattinam in Thoothukudi district recorded 18cm of rain in the 24 hours ending Thursday morning. Following overnight showers that inundated school premises, district collector Vishu Mahajan declared a holiday for schools in Tiruchendur taluk on Thursday.Waterlogging was reported near Mutharamman temple, the police station and arterial roads in Kulasekarapattinam, inconveniencing motorists and devotees. Udangudi, Manapad and several other coastal villages also received heavy rainfall.In Tirunelveli, intermittent showers continued into Thursday evening. Heavy rain in the Western Ghats triggered a rise in water levels near Manimuthar, prompting authorities to restrict tourist access.In neighbouring Tenkasi, bathing at Courtallam Main Falls was prohibited following a sharp increase in water flow.The restriction disappointed Sabarimala pilgrims who traditionally stop at the falls to bathe on their way to Kerala. However, tourists were allowed to bathe at Five Falls, Old Courtallam and some smaller waterfalls on Thursday morning.The rainfall brought some relief to reservoirs across southern Tamil Nadu, with Papanasam and Manimuthar dams receiving more water than they released. Pechiparai and Perunchani reservoirs in Kanyakumari district also recorded fresh inflows.However, water storage in several major reservoirs remained considerably below last year's levels. Storage in Mullaperiyar and Vaigai continued to decline, with Vaigai holding only 39% of its capacity.The showers are significant for the region, where Madurai and Theni had recorded seasonal rainfall deficits of 34% and 23%, respectively, until Tuesday. The shortfall has raised concerns over water availability for irrigation and drinking purposes.While southern and western Tamil Nadu are expected to receive further showers, Chennai and neighbouring districts may see only isolated light rainfall spells for the remainder of November.V R Durai, director of the Area Cyclone Warning Centre at the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, said the easterly trough that was expected to bring rainfall to Tamil Nadu had shifted westwards, taking rain-bearing activity towards Kerala.“There is no possibility for rainfall over north TN, including Chennai, at least till the end of Nov,” he said.According to the IMD forecast, heavy rain is likely at isolated places in the Ghat areas of Theni on Friday (November 27). Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 30-40kmph are likely at one or two places across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal until Saturday (November 28).On November 28, moderate rain is likely over the delta, southern and western districts, while isolated light showers may occur elsewhere. North Tamil Nadu and some delta and central districts may remain largely dry on November 29.Light rain is forecast at isolated places over north coastal Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 30. Moderate showers are likely over coastal Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on December 1, while southern and delta districts are expected to receive moderate rain on December 2. Light rain may occur over the remaining parts of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.Durai said a low-pressure area was also likely to form over the south Andaman Sea, but its eventual movement remained uncertain. Forecast models could change as the system develops, he added.Chennai is likely to record a maximum temperature of 31-32°C and a minimum of 24-25°C on Friday.Tamil Nadu has so far recorded a 15% deficit in northeast monsoon rainfall. The shortfall is particularly pronounced in Chengalpet (51%), Kancheepuram (43%), Chennai (32%) and Tiruvallur (21%).
Article Summary: Heavy rain expected in the Ghat areas of Theni district on Friday. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to continue across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal until Saturday. Warning comes as the northeast monsoon regained strength over southern Tamil Nadu on Thursday.
